## Question 1 (4 points)

Let $X_i \sim N(20, 2)$ for $i = 1,2, \dots, 50$ and assume these are independent. What are the following?

-   $\text{E}[20\bar{X} + 4]$
-   $\text{SD}[30\bar{X} - 5]$

## Question 2A (9 points)

Let $X_i \sim N(10, 3)$ and $Y_i \sim N(20, 4)$ for $i = 1, 2, 3, \dots, 30$ and assume independence between all $X_i$ and $Y_i$. What is the sampling distribution of $\bar{X} + \bar{Y}$? Replace the $a$, $b$ and $c$ in the formula below with the correct values.

$$
\bar{X} + \bar{Y} \sim N\left(a, \frac{b}{\sqrt{c}} \right)
$$

Hint: Find the sampling distributions of $\bar{X}$ and $\bar{Y}$ first and then use the theorems regarding the expectation and variance of a linear combination of two independent random variables. Also, be sure to be careful when distinguishing between variance and standard deviation when applying these theorems.

## Question 2B (5 points)

Complete the code block below to simulate draws from the sampling distribution of $\bar{X} + \bar{Y}$ from the previous question. Then compute the mean and standard deviation of the simulated draws and create a histogram of the draws.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
set.seed(100)

n_draws <- 100000 # Number of draws/simulations
n <- 30 # Sample size
xybars <- rep(0, n_draws) # Vector to stores draws for sum of sample means

mu_X <- 10
mu_Y <- 20
sigma_X <- 3
sigma_Y <- 4

for (i in 1:n_draws){
  x_sample <- rnorm(n, 0, 1) # Replace the 0 and 1 with the appropriate values/variables
  y_sample <- rnorm(n, 0, 1) # Replace the 0 and 1 with the appropriate values/variables
  
  xbar <- mean(x_sample)
  ybar <- mean(y_sample)
  xybars[i] <- 0 + 0 # Replace the 0 and 0 with the appropriate variables
}

mean(xybars)
sd(xybars)

hist(xybars)
```
